headline: Highest risk is medium: dbt-core can egress to a data warehouse while marker is local-only, creating a plausible data-handling and workflow-conflict pair with limited direct evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. dbt-core only calls a data warehouse and has allowlisted egress, while marker has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces. Without a bridge, marker cannot inject instructions into dbt-core by default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies marker output into dbt-core prompts or configs, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not paste marker output into dbt-core configuration without review.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to a warehouse, but marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not a likely exfiltration source. The main risk is accidental exposure through shared inputs, which is not documented here and appears limited.
conditions: IF marker is given warehouse exports or sensitive documents as input, it may process them locally.
IF dbt-core is configured to emit warehouse contents into files later consumed by another system, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid feeding sensitive warehouse extracts into marker.
Restrict dbt-core to non-sensitive schemas during testing.
Review any file handoff between the tools before execution.
requires-engineering: add data-class filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A write-conflict pathway is provably blocked by profile B: marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. dbt-core also has no write or git capabilities listed. With no overlapping mutable surface, capability conflict is not plausible by default.
conditions: IF marker is replaced with a version that can write files or modify git state, conflict risk changes.
IF dbt-core is wrapped in an orchestrator that grants shared mutable storage, the pathway may open.
mitigations: Do not grant dbt-core shared write access to the same directory.
requires-engineering: add locking if either agent gains write access.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-derived outputs that marker may consume as documents, so a downstream workflow could treat dbt-generated content as authoritative. Marker has no built-in verification or action-taking controls in the profile, making silent propagation plausible even though direct automation is not shown.
conditions: IF marker is used to summarize dbt-core outputs without human review, errors can cascade.
IF dbt-core outputs are copied into reports or tickets that drive decisions, downstream action risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review of dbt outputs before marker summarizes them.
Add a verification checklist for any facts passed from dbt-core to marker.
Label dbt-derived text as untrusted until checked.
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance checks in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which can implicate residency or retention controls, but marker has no documented data classes or compliance-specific surfaces. The pair does not show a direct mismatch; the main issue is that dbt-core may process regulated warehouse data while marker remains a generic local processor.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is routed through marker, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the warehouse contains EU PII or PHI and marker is used in the same workflow, policy review is required.
mitigations: Confirm the data class before routing outputs to marker.
Exclude regulated datasets from the shared workflow.
Document retention and deletion handling for dbt artifacts.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
